sentences.text: An isolation boundary defines the equipment and energy sources that must be made safe before field work begins.
The boundary is approved against the task scope, current equipment configuration, and applicable operating constraints.
The Work Permit Portal makes the approved boundary available to the work party and the control team.
The approval identifies each isolation point, the required device position, and the person responsible for applying the control.
It also records any adjacent equipment that must remain energized or available for service.
The Electrical Technician uses the boundary sketch to identify the approved isolation points before starting the work.
The Field Supervisor briefs the crew on the boundary, access restrictions, and conditions that require work to stop.
The Control Engineer checks that remote indications agree with the approved switching state before authorizing access.
Where local indication is required, a qualified technician checks the device at the point of isolation.
The work party confirms equipment identity using permanent labels and the current site designation.
A mismatch between the field label and the approved record prevents the crew from proceeding until it is resolved.
Each isolation device is secured against unintended operation using the site-approved locking and tagging method.
Personal protection is applied in accordance with the permit and local electrical safety rules.
Electrical absence-of-voltage checks are performed at the work location using suitable, tested equipment.
Stored energy, induced voltage, and other hazardous energy sources are assessed before hands-on work begins.
The Field Supervisor confirms that every crew member understands the limits of the approved work area.
Changes to the task, equipment state, or work location require a review of the boundary before work continues.
The Work Permit Portal retains the current approval and makes superseded versions unavailable for active work.
Control room staff and the field team use the same revision when confirming isolation status.
A shift handover records outstanding isolations, affected equipment, and any restrictions that remain in force.
The incoming team independently checks the boundary status before accepting responsibility for ongoing work.
No isolation is removed until the work is complete, personnel and tools are accounted for, and the responsible authority approves restoration.
The person removing each control confirms that the associated work party is clear of the hazard area.
The Control Engineer verifies the restoration state and communicates any remaining operational limitation to affected personnel.
Boundary records are closed only after the equipment state has been confirmed and the permit has been updated.
